scores.justification: No notable weaknesses; the implementation thoroughly anticipates and resolves edge cases and cross-module state desynchronisation, such as `syncRequestsWithParcels()` cleaning up requests when parcels are completed or marked missing in Task 1, and `processNextRequest()` verifying Task 3 resource availability before dequeuing.

scores.criterion: Use of appropriate data structures and algorithms
scores.justification: While the custom `ServicePriorityQueue` and `ServiceRequestStore` linked list are well-structured, `ServiceRequestStore` uses O(n) linear scans for `find()` and `activeForParcel()`, and `ServicePriorityQueue::enqueue` ignores the `sequence` field when restoring from file, relying only on insertion order.

All five functional requirements for Task 2 (creating, maintaining, prioritizing, processing/updating, and handling exceptional conditions) are completely and accurately implemented with no visible gaps.

scores.criterion: Code quality: readability, efficiency and correctness
scores.justification: The code is clean, well-modularised, and adheres to good C++ practices including proper destructor memory management and deleted copy constructors (`ServicePriorityQueue(const ServicePriorityQueue&) = delete`).

scores.criterion: Quality of individual contribution to the integrated system
scores.justification: Task 2 integrates seamlessly with Tasks 1, 3, and 4 via clean interfaces (`createServiceRequest`, `getActiveRequestID`, `releaseResourceFor`, and `logActivity`) as well as contributing shared utilities in `Common.hpp`.

scores.criterion: Innovation and creativity in the solution
scores.justification: The inclusion of fault-tolerant file persistence (`saveServiceRequests` and `loadServiceRequests` with format validation and orphan checking) and automatic cross-module synchronisation (`syncRequestsWithParcels` and `refreshRecipientDetails`) goes well beyond basic prototype expectations.
